commit.message: Merge fix-all (b4504ab; lead): every finding of the 2026-10-06 whole-code assessment fixed, and tools/validate.py (the device against a CPU Hugging Face golden with openTPU's quantization), production since 2026-10-07 06:52 (opentpu: deploy_fixall_84989047, build 84989047, host 9bc1ffa, prev fpfix e776703a). Board RTL (fix-board): otpu_mem_ch's write-accept counts cross per controller port with a signed B check gated on WLAST; otpu_axil_iso and the CSR crossing's reset with the sys reset; XADC DCLK from core_clk (ADCCLK 22.22 MHz); the loader waits for read idle and core_rst for both idles; WAITW's timeout only between reads; HALTED after the units stop; STREAMS=0 makes DSTEP / STREAM illegal; STATUS bit 9 ECC_DED (sticky); RUN / LOAD refused while uncalibrated; TEMP ungated; the trace count keeps its low bits. Core / ISA (fix-core): STREAM's destination in the scoreboard footprint, QST's footprint in whole beats, 2^32 saturation, MM N, KB >= 1. Compiler (fix-compiler): attention's masked last block stops at cap, register reuse (_free_for, zero_head, late_zero), the LOOP rule at issue, QST / GATHER overlap checks, check_live, progcache keyed on host/offload.py. Host (fix-host): quiesce / stop on every exit path, SIGTERM / SIGHUP through cleanup, otpu-lock signal forwarding + PDEATHSIG + OTPU_LOCK_PID, unaligned writes beat by beat (MTP state words 32..40), bounded waits, offload seq rebase, /tmp/otpu for several users, Board.start / Board.wait checks (RUN taken, ECC_DED), tools/qual/runend.py. LLM (fix-llm): host sampler softcap, top_p <= 0, generate_batch, RoPE / sliding / attention-bias refusals, generation_config defaults. Qual (fix-qual): the build checked on the card (EXPECT / REST_EXPECT), exit status, references format 2 (32 tokens past EOS, logits sha256 + top-5, a long LFM2 prompt across the 256 bucket), the rtlsim build cache, the TMEM dump. validate-hf: tools/validate.py (isa / rtl / board, --against a device or a saved card run, Gemma 4), README 'Validating against Hugging Face'. Lead: per-session pytest basetemp, turnaround.py's ECC wording, qual.sh's sha of a staged tree. Build (opentpu, 133.33 MHz, Gen2): all constraints met, WNS +0.058 / WHS +0.013, core_clk +0.125, LiteDRAM sys +0.105, the same CDC criticals as fpfix, sha256 439e942e0f302533abb9a891cd31c48d51528760da7f222a4b01c24c6a57a499. Card (2026-10-07 06:12-06:53): fpcard 5 / 5, runend 3 / 3, qual fast QUAL EXIT 0 (53 PASS, eight format-2 references bit-exact incl. resident, prompt runs and the card loop), device Mcycles/token equal to fpfix's, validate.py card runs (6) bit-exact with the ISA simulator and KL 0.95 - 1.25x the golden's floor, WAITW tag rounds, BIST, H2C stress flags 0, ECC 0, warm reboots after load / restore clean; promote.sh PROMOTE PASS. Gates: omarchy RTL units 290, board model 159, autodecode rtl 26 passed (8498904); board model 159 passed (9bc1ffa); Mac tests -k 'not rtl and not board_model' 1173 passed, 40 skipped, 0 failed (9bc1ffa).

README: validate.py on the card (build 84989047): Qwen3-0.6B, LFM2.5-230M and Qwen3.5-0.8B in int8 and 4-bit, the card's tokens and logits bit-identical to the ISA simulator's on every prompt, its KL from the quantized golden 0.95 - 1.25x the floor

Merge fix-host (18aaa8a): a locked Board quiesces a run left going (waits for HALTED, CTRL=0, WR_IDLE; OTPU_STOP_RUN=1 cuts it short) and every error / exit path stops the card; SIGTERM / SIGHUP end card holders through their cleanup; otpu-lock forwards signals and waits for its command (PDEATHSIG), OTPU_LOCK_HELD checked against a live ancestor holding the flock (OTPU_LOCK_PID); unaligned writes beat by beat (the stop word's beat holds host words only; MTP's state words move to 32..40); bounded waits (RUN_TIMEOUT, serving loops, DQS move) and a WR_IDLE timeout is an error; offload seq rebased below 2^23 between runs; /tmp/otpu safe for several users; BoardDram writes only touched beats; CHASH-aware logits probe; SNAP snapshots retried; Board.start refuses a run the card did not take (uncalibrated), Board.wait raises on ECC_DED during a run; tools/qual/runend.py card check

Merge validate-hf (c7b6f95): tools/validate.py runs Gemma 4 (the image's formats, the head rows as the embedding, the device's PLE records, H^-0.5 folded into the PLE projection; logits compared after the soft cap; HF's language model alone, bf16-held weights widened per Linear: 16.1 GB peak). E2B on the ISA simulator: int8 KL 1.02x the floor, fp4 / int8 head 0.82x, PASS; gemma4.Weights reads text-only checkpoints

tools/validate.py: Gemma 4 (E2B, E4B) against Hugging Face. The golden takes the device image's formats (gemma4.Image follows the card's fit: E2B's int8 image has its PLE table in 4-bit; image_formats, kept in --save / --json), the embedding rows from the LM head in the head's format (the device gathers them from the head), the per-layer embeddings from the device's PLE records (dequant_records; the table's rows read from the checkpoint as needed), the PLE projection's weight with 1 / sqrt(H) folded in as the image quantizes it, int8 activations per 128 at every Linear input, attention as _attend_heads, and it compares the logits after the soft cap (the device's are before it). Memory: Hugging Face builds Gemma4ForCausalLM from the text config without the PLE table (E2B's is 9.4 GB in fp32) and gets the checkpoint's tensors one at a time (gemma4.load_weights); the golden keeps bf16-exact weights in bf16 and widens them a matrix at a time for its fp32 passes. gemma4.Weights reads a text-only checkpoint's names (model.*, lm_head.*) as they are. The MoE models are refused (unsupported(): Gemma 4 26B-A4B too). run_device also returns the image's formats; the KV cap rounds to whole 256-token buckets. Measured on omarchy, ISA simulator (board_config, MCOLS=4), 8 prompts x 16 tokens: E2B int8 (PLE table 4-bit): device vs W+A top-1 100.0%, KL 3.55e-3 = 1.02x the floor's 3.48e-3, device vs fp32 99.2% / 1.51e-2, W+A vs fp32 1.67e-2, PASS, 950 s; fp4 with an int8 head (PLE table int8): 99.2%, 2.94e-3 = 0.82x the floor's 3.59e-3, device vs fp32 96.9% / 4.47e-2, W+A vs fp32 4.34e-2, PASS, 1531 s (the host shared); both peak at 16.1 GB RSS. README: the Gemma 4 rows and its memory need (16 GB peak, 22 GB free). test_validate: the quantized golden follows the ISA simulator on a tiny Gemma 4 (sliding and global layers, KV-shared layers, PLE) in int8 and fp4; the command line on a tiny Gemma 4 checkpoint (fp4: head fp4, PLE table int8, PASS; on the old gemma4.Weights it fails to load the text-only checkpoint).

Merge validate-hf (62fdf13): the emulation's _fake_q rounds exact ties as fp32.quantize does (Gemma 4's fp4 head rows reach .5 ties at the PLE projection's int8 point; the device was right: HF's Gemma 4 forward on the image's own inputs matches the ISA simulator to 8e-7)

Board on fix-board's RTL: start() checks that the card took RUN, wait() raises on an ECC error during the run, stop()'s 1 ms only for older bitstreams

- start(): STATUS after RUN; RUN still clear (CTRL takes neither RUN nor LOAD while CALIB0 /
  CALIB1 are not both set) raises, naming the uncalibrated channel, instead of a wait that
  polls HALTED until its timeout (RUN_TIMEOUT). One register read per run; not on the board
  model (a script).
- wait(): STATUS ECC_DED (bit 9, sticky until the ECC counters' clear: Board.scrub) set
  during the run raises after the run is stopped (after ERROR and AXI_ERR); set before it
  (the same STATUS read as start's), stats["ecc_ded"] says so and the Board warns once on
  stderr. Not in QUIET.
- stop(): CTRL = 0 and WR_IDLE are the whole sequence on fix-board's RTL (docs/observability.md,
  "Stopping a run": the loader and RUN wait for the adapter's reads); CUT_SETTLE stays for a
  cut-short run on older bitstreams.
- FakeTransport: calib (CTRL takes RUN / LOAD only with both, as the RTL) and ecc_ded.
- test_board's run_h2c stub answers STATUS RUN.

Tests: test_host_runs: a run on an uncalibrated card is refused at its start, an ECC error
during a run is an error (both fail on 2d5870c with the new FakeTransport: no raise,
KeyError ecc_ded). docs/host.md "Ending a run" and a paragraph on both.

emulated_logits: an exact rounding tie rounds as the device's quantizer rounds it (_fake_q: fp32.quantize on the block in fp32, x * 127 recip(amax)), not half to even. Gemma 4's emulation was 0.5-1% off the device in fp4 with per-layer inputs at about half of the tiny model's positions: a 4-bit LM head's rows (the embedding rows) quantize to int8 at the PLE projection's input with exact ties (fp4 codes 3 and 6 make 63.5; 12751 ties in the tiny's 1000 rows, 566 rows with one the device rounds the other way). The device was right: Hugging Face's Gemma 4 forward with the device's weights (quantize_mxu, dequantized), embedding rows, PLE records (pack_records, dequantized) and quantizer (fp32.quantize at every Linear input; attention as _attend_heads) is the ISA simulator's to 8e-7 at every position (one global layer, fp4, 12 tokens; the per-layer inputs to 7e-7), and the emulation was off at the 6 positions whose token's row has such a tie. Now the emulation is the device's to 2e-7 at every position there. On the 9-layer tiny its per-layer inputs are the device's to 2e-7 at every position; its logits part from the second position on at a rounding decision in attention (an exact tie in a flash block's output, an integer vector times a scalar, that the device decides in its fp32 attention arithmetic, or an fp32 near tie), as Hugging Face's do one position later. formats_scan check and the Gemma 4 twins still equal (2.7e-15, 1.4e-15). test_gemma4: test_emulation_rounds_ties_as_the_device (every fp4 row's int8 values fp32.quantize's; emulated_logits the ISA simulator's to 1e-5 of the largest on one global layer with per-layer inputs; fails on the unfixed tree), the tiny model's builder _model.

Merge fix-compiler: attention's masked last block stops at cap (partial buckets: resident decode, prompt runs and the device decode loop were NaN or wrong at caps not a multiple of 256); address registers never reused with a run-time value from a still-running loop or a 0-count device loop (and scratch() of a released argument); progcache key hashes host/offload.py; isasim checks the nested-LOOP rule at issue whatever the count (compiler NOP after raw guards); isa.py ValueError checks, isasim QST / GATHER overlap checks, resolved GATHER dst agreement, check_live in reduce / all_gather / store_quantized, Tile views. Real-model programs unchanged (768 dense + MoE + tiny at cap 4096, card config)

tests/conftest.py IsaCard: a late piece that ends inside a 128-byte beat pair carries the bytes after it as the run left them, not zeros. A late region of one row of logits (4 * vocab bytes, vocab not a multiple of 32) ends inside one, and the zero pad cleared the start of the next row, which the run had written at once. test_host: a 10-token prefill (runs of 8 and 2 rows: the logits are row 1's) on the fake card with vocab 1000 gives the ISA simulator's logits (on the old fake row 1's first 24 logits read 0: fails). test_validate's card test: the workaround (the late region cut to whole beats) dropped.

emulated_logits: P V as the device's flash attention takes it (kernels/attention.py _attend_heads): V as int8 values and one scale per token, the scales folded into the softmax numerators before P is quantized per D keys (QACT CSCALE), against V's int8 values (qwen3 _v_parts, _pv; qwen3, lfm2, qwen35, gemma4 and the tools' copies: formats_scan._attend, gemma4_quant_eval.emulate, offload/emul_step.py). The emulation quantized P alone against V dequantized per token, about 1% off the device. With the fold a flash block's attention output is an integer vector times a scalar and its quantization has exact .5 ties, which float64 noise broke differently in the batched and the per-token emulations (formats_scan check: SmolLM3's int8 row 1.6e-2 off): _fake_q rounds a value within 2^-31 of a tie half to even, and the twins are equal again (formats_scan check: worst logits rel 2.7e-15; gemma4_quant_eval check's three formats on the tiny Gemma 4: 1.5e-15). test_validate: emulated_logits against the ISA simulator with fp4 weights on tiny Qwen3 / LFM2 / Qwen3.5 (two prompts, the prefill and 7 steps), the logits to fp32 rounding: 1.5e-7, 1.4e-7, 2.0e-7 of the largest (the unfolded emulation 1.3e-2, 1.4e-2, 1.0e-2: the three fail on the unfixed tree).

otpu_tmem: the simulation's TMEM dump is the memory itself (the first copy's block RAMs, every other copy checked against them), not a shadow of the write requests

The tmem_<SID>.hex that assert_same_state, test_fp_rtl and test_vops compare was a flat shadow
written from bw_* (the selected writes, before the registered write stage): a defect in pw_*,
the RAM's addressing or a replica's write showed only if a later instruction read the word, and
test_rtl's fuzzers write fresh TMEM destinations nothing reads again. Now on dump the first
copy's banks (DP) copy their words into img; a cycle later every other copy is compared with
them (a difference stops the simulation with the copy, word and both values) and img is
written. +tmem_fault=<SID>,<word> (+tmem_fault_port=<port>) flips bit 0 of every write to the
word as it lands in every copy (one copy's): the tests' fault in the write stage / RAM.
Simulation only: with SYNTHESIS defined the preprocessed module is the same text as before
(verilator -E -DSYNTHESIS, comments stripped), so no timing change. Verilator lint of otpu_top
and otpu_board: no new warnings.
Test: test_rtl.py test_tmem_dump_is_the_ram (fails on main's RTL: the dump does not see the
flipped word, and a copy that differs passes); with the fuzzers 14 passed (Mac)

test_autodecode: the decode loop on the device at a partial last bucket (cap 384: bucket 2's masked block the cache's last 128 tokens) gives the per-position programs' tokens across 256 for Qwen3, LFM2 and Qwen3.5, every KV region followed by -NaN words (on main the first token of bucket 2 is 0: NaN logits)

validate.py's bound is the floor: the device's mean KL from the quantized golden at most 3x the golden's own against a 1-ulp nudge of its inputs (--kl-ratio; or --max-kl, 1e-3), top-1 at least 80% (--min-top1). Once one int8 value rounds the other way the difference spreads through the later layers, so the golden cannot sit closer to the device than to itself; measured on the ISA simulator (omarchy, board_config, 8 prompts x 16 tokens): Qwen3-0.6B, LFM2.5-230M, Qwen3.5-0.8B in int8 and fp4 + int8 head, the device at 0.84-1.16x the floor (KL 0.0020-0.0155), its distance from fp32 the quantization's own (W+A vs fp32 within 0.8-1.25x). README: Validating against Hugging Face (the commands for the ISA simulator, the RTL and the card, the rows, the measured table). test_validate: the card path (run_device on BoardBackend over conftest's IsaCard) against the isa path, bit for bit.

test_run_dropped_then_load_and_run_at_once: drops at 600, 1300 and 2500 cycles

On main's RTL the drops at 600 and 1300 (during the first LD's reads) hang the second program
(STATUS 0xe8: RUN, no HALTED, at the board model's cycle cap); 2500 and 4000 pass there (no read
in flight). The fixed RTL passes all.

memch_test: a synchronized count's sample is never ahead of its count; write-only skew scenarios

otpu_mem_ch's skew model (sim only) now errors when a first-stage sample decodes ahead of the
count it samples, the invariant one-bit steps keep. New scenarios skeww (ldn) and gen2skeww
(xreg): XDMA writing only, unstalled, the controller model busy half the time, so both ports
take XDMA writes in one cycle more often. On the fixed RTL skew, skewsh, skeww, gen2skew,
gen2skewx and gen2skeww pass. Mutations 33-35 (a count summed over both ports before it crosses,
the bug dc5b486 fixed) are caught: xreg gen2skeww "XDMA's beats taken (144) behind its answered
bursts' (145)" (a B before its beat was taken) and skeww "x_wacc's sample 595 ahead of the
count, 594"; ldn skew / skewsh / skeww ahead-errors for x_wacc and a_wacc (gen2skew alone missed
mutation 33 at its seed).

otpu-lock: OTPU_LOCK_HELD stays the bare device name, its pid goes in OTPU_LOCK_PID

<dev>:<pid> broke mixing trees: an older tree's tools under the new otpu-lock compared the
variable with the device name and took the lock (DeviceBusy), and the new tools under an older
otpu-lock (the card host's installed one) saw no pid. A tool now checks the pid the lock file
names (every otpu-lock writes its own there; OTPU_LOCK_PID's when set): an ancestor that holds
the flock. Checked both ways with 982d668's tree.

tools/qual/runend.py: the card check of how runs end (Board.stop, quiesce, SIGTERM)

Three checks for the lead's card session (not run: no card access here), each a [PASS] / [FAIL]
line: a run with 16 KiB LD / ST in flight cut short by Board.stop leaves STATUS RUN clear and QUIET
set, and the demo then runs bit for bit as the ISA simulator (checks.run_demo: no stale port B read
in IMEM, no late write over it); a holder SIGKILLed mid-run leaves its run to the next open, which
refuses it after QUIESCE_WAIT (2 s here) and cuts it short with OTPU_STOP_RUN=1, the demo passing
after; a holder sent SIGTERM mid-run exits 143 with RUN clear. Run under otpu-lock.

XADC: DCLK_FREQUENCY from core_clk, and build.tcl checks ADCCLK

The XADC's DCLK is core_clk, but the block design told the wizard 100 MHz: its divider of 4 ran
ADCCLK at 33 MHz at core_clk 133.33 MHz (DS182: at most 26 MHz). bd_native.tcl now gives
CORE_HZ in whole MHz rounded up (134 at 133.33: a divider of 6, 22.2 MHz). build.tcl writes
"XADC ADCCLK <MHz> (DCLK / <divider>)" to SUMMARY.txt from the netlist's INIT_42 and DCLK's
clock, with a CRITICAL WARNING above 26 MHz or when it cannot check. Tcl syntax checked
(make lint); the wizard's divider and the SUMMARY line need the next build.
